subject: Weekly leadership spotlight: priority lanes, QBR asks and decision lanes
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: qbr@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 07:12:00 -0000
Subject: Weekly leadership spotlight: priority lanes, QBR asks and decision lanes

Team —

Quick leadership snapshot to align ahead of next week’s QBR with Acme. I focused this week on three compact sections (Wins / Risks / Asks) and a short decision lane table at the bottom. Please review and flag anything that needs to move up the stack. I’ve attached the latest QBR deck draft and our SLA/ask spreadsheet for procurement.

Wins
- Redwood Dedicated: Canary for the new batching optimizer deployed; 18% avg token-cost reduction observed on a subset of Acme workloads (M-F 9–17 PST).
- Console: Trial telemetry retention extended to 90 days for the Acme pilot without material storage cost impact.
- Evals: Two critical prompt regressions identified and triaged; fixes in model config are staged.

Risks / Hotspots
- Capacity: We’re seeing a higher-than-expected tail latency for long-turn chats when prefix caching misses — risk to Acme SLO if traffic spikes during their marketing event (Apr 16–18). Engineering is reprioritizing a KV cache hotfix but it’s not yet in canary.
- Contracting: Procurement at Acme has signaled a tighter timeline; they requested final SLAs + IP/data handling language by EOW (Apr 16). If we miss that, signing could slip into May.
- Rollout: The new quantized model variant shows subtle hallucination regressions on domain-specific prompts; further prompt engineering mitigation required before broad promotion.

Asks (who / what / by when)
- Engineering (Karthik): Please prioritize the KV cache hotfix canary and provide a rollout ETA; need canary in production by Apr 13 to be confident for Acme’s event.
- Product (Laura): Consolidate the QBR narrative (1 slide) that explains our cost/latency trade-offs and fallback strategy for the event; share a 1-pager by Mon Apr 12 EOD.
- Sales/CS (Jonas & Soojin): Confirm customer comms timing and whether Acme needs a short during-event escalation channel; commit to the message by Mon Apr 12.
- Legal/Contracts (cc’ing procurement): Please review the SLA table in sla-asklist.xlsx and flag any redlines by Apr 15.

Decision lanes (short)
- If KV hotfix ETA > Apr 13: approve temporary capacity bump and canary routing to avoid SLO breaches (decision: leadership ops).
- If hallucination rate on quantized variant > 2% after prompt mitigations: hold promotion and extend existing variant for Acme by default (decision: product + research).

Attachments: QBR-draft-v2.pdf (deck), sla-asklist.xlsx (procurement items).

I’ll collect replies inline; suggest any edits to the deck link below.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: qbr@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 08:43:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership spotlight: priority lanes, QBR asks and decision lanes

Thanks, Irene — good concise framing. I uploaded a refreshed one-slide narrative and annotated speaker notes into the deck (see Drive link). High-level edits: tightened the event mitigation slide, moved the fallback routing callout up front, and added the executive escalation contact.

Two quick clarifications for the asks list:
1) Procurement redlines: Acme asked that we include a standard data residency paragraph for logs. Legal will weigh in, but I recommend a single-sentence commitment with exceptions called out — avoids broad commitments in the deck.
2) Regarding the hallucination mitigation: could research share a short summary of the prompt adjustments (2–3 bullets) so we can include as a mitigation step in the QBR slide?

Attachment: QBR-draft-v2.pdf (Irene, I used your deck and applied the edits directly).

Laura Bennett
Chief Product Officer
Redwood Inference
